ai.literal: to the lover / not granting / I agreed / paled / my / nature - to whom / shall I tell / else
ai.translation: I myself consented to my lover's departure. To whom else can I now complain about my paled state?
ai.modern: என் காதலர் என்னைப் பிரிந்து செல்வதற்கு நானே சம்மதித்தேன். இப்போது பசலை நோய் அடைந்த என் நிலையை வேறு யாரிடம் சொல்வேன்?
ai.explanation: The heroine laments her situation, realizing she is the cause of her own suffering. She had agreed to her lover's departure, which is described as 'not granting' his continued presence. Because she consented to the separation, she feels she has no right to complain to anyone else about the pallor that has now afflicted her body. The word 'piṟa' emphasizes her helplessness, asking who else could possibly listen to a self-inflicted sorrow.

ai.literal: He gave, saying, by the pride, spreading having done, my body upon crawls pallor.
ai.translation: With the proud thought that 'He gave me,' the pallor spreads and crawls all over my body.
ai.modern: தலைவர் எனக்கு இதைக் கொடுத்தார் என்னும் பெருமையால், பசப்பு என் உடம்பின் மேல் ஏறிப் பரவுகிறது.
ai.explanation: The heroine playfully personifies her pallor, the yellowing of her skin caused by lovesickness. She imagines that the pallor is proud because it was given to her directly by her lover when he departed. Swelling with this pride, the pallor eagerly climbs and spreads all over her body. The word 'தகை' here means pride or boastfulness, capturing the poetic conceit of the spreading color.

ai.literal: Grace and modesty he took, as exchange pain and pallor having given.
ai.translation: He took away my grace and modesty, giving me the pain of longing and a sickly pallor in exchange.
ai.modern: அவர் என் மென்மையையும் நாணத்தையும் எடுத்துக்கொண்டு, அதற்குப் பதிலாக காதல் நோயையும் பசலை நிறத்தையும் தந்துவிட்டார்.
ai.explanation: The speaker laments the physical and emotional toll of her lover's departure. She says he has taken away her natural grace ('சாயல்') and her modesty ('நாண்'). In return ('கைம்மாறா'), he has left her with the pain of separation ('நோய்') and a sickly pallor ('பசலை'). The couplet uses the image of an unfair exchange to highlight how love has stripped her of her best qualities and replaced them with suffering.

ai.literal: Think-will-I indeed, I; speak-that-which his nature indeed; deceit other-? pallor.
ai.translation: I think of him constantly, and what I speak of is his nature. Is this pallor that still afflicts me deceitful, or something else?
ai.modern: நான் அவரை எப்போதும் நினைக்கிறேன்; நான் பேசுவதும் அவருடைய குணங்களைப் பற்றித்தான். அப்படியிருக்க, என் மேல் படரும் இந்தப் பசப்பு நிறம் பொய்யானதா அல்லது வேறு ஏதாவதா?
ai.explanation: The speaker wonders why she suffers from the pallor of separation when her lover is constantly in her thoughts and words. Since he is always present in her mind and speech, she feels they are not truly separated. Therefore, she questions whether the pallor that appears on her body is merely a deceitful illusion or something else entirely, as it contradicts her inner experience of his presence.

ai.literal: Look yonder, my lover goes; look here, on my body pallor spreading.
ai.translation: Look yonder, my lover is departing! Look here, pallor is already spreading over my body.
ai.modern: அதோ பார், என் காதலர் செல்கிறார்; இதோ பார், என் உடம்பில் பசலை நிறம் படர்கிறது.
ai.explanation: The heroine expresses her sorrow at her lover's departure by pointing out the immediate physical effect it has on her. She tells her friend to look yonder at her lover who is walking away. In the very next breath, she tells her to look here at her own body, where the pale hue of separation is already spreading. The contrast between yonder (உவக்காண்) and here (இவக்காண்) emphasizes how instantly the grief of separation manifests as physical pallor.

ai.literal: Lamp's fading waiting for darkness-indeed like, lover's embrace gap waiting for pallor.
ai.translation: Just as darkness waits for the lamp to fade, pallor waits for a gap in my lover's embrace.
ai.modern: விளக்கின் ஒளி குறைவதற்காக இருள் காத்திருப்பதைப் போல, என் காதலனின் தழுவல் விலகும் நேரத்திற்காக இந்தப் பசலை நோய் காத்திருக்கிறது.
ai.explanation: The couplet compares the onset of lovesickness to the behavior of darkness. Darkness constantly hovers, waiting for the exact moment a lamp's light fades to rush in and take over. Similarly, the heroine feels that the sickly pallor of separation is always lurking, waiting for the slightest gap or loosening in her lover's embrace to instantly cover her body. The word 'அற்றம்' is used beautifully to mean both the fading vulnerability of the lamp and the physical gap in the embrace.

ai.literal: Embracing I lay, I turned aside; in that moment, scooping up taking nature indeed pallor.
ai.translation: I lay in his embrace and merely turned to the side. In that brief moment, pallor rushed upon me so thickly it could be scooped up in handfuls.
ai.modern: நான் அவரைத் தழுவிக்கொண்டு கிடந்தேன், சிறிது பக்கவாட்டில் திரும்பினேன். அந்தச் சிறு நேரத்திற்குள், அள்ளிக்கொள்ளும் அளவுக்குப் பசலை நிறம் என் மேல் படர்ந்துவிட்டது.
ai.explanation: The speaker describes the extreme sensitivity of her love and the swiftness of her physical reaction to even the slightest separation. She was lying in her lover's embrace and merely turned her body to the side. In that split second, the pallor of separation ('pacappu') rushed over her body so thickly that it felt as though it could be scooped up in handfuls ('aḷḷikkoḷ'). The imagery highlights how deeply intertwined her physical state is with his immediate physical contact, where even a momentary shift in posture feels like abandonment.

ai.literal: "She grew pale", saying except, her abandoned he, those who say are not.
ai.translation: People only say, "She has grown pale," but no one says, "He abandoned her."
ai.modern: "இவள் பசலை நோய் கொண்டு நிறம் மாறினாள்" என்று ஊரார் சொல்வார்களே தவிர, "அவர் இவளை விட்டுப் பிரிந்து சென்றார்" என்று அவர் மேல் தவறு சொல்வார் யாரும் இல்லை.
ai.explanation: The heroine laments the unfairness of the townspeople's gossip. They are quick to notice her pallor and blame her for not bearing the separation gracefully. However, no one points out the root cause of her suffering or blames the hero for abandoning her. The contrast between "என்பது அல்லால்" (other than saying) and "என்பார் இல்" (there is no one who says) highlights her isolation and the one-sided nature of society's judgment.

ai.literal: let it turn pale indeed as it happens my body he who caused desire he who is in a good state he will be if
ai.translation: Let my body turn pale as it naturally would, if the one who made me love him remains in a good state.
ai.modern: என்னை விரும்பச் செய்த என் காதலர் நல்ல நிலையில் இருப்பார் என்றால், என் உடல் அதன் இயல்புப்படி பசலை நிறம் அடையட்டும்.
ai.explanation: The heroine speaks to her friend about her pallor, which appears due to her lover's absence. She declares that she does not mind her body turning pale, as long as her lover, who first sparked her desire, is safe and well. The word 'நயப்பித்தார்' highlights that he was the one who initiated their love, making her current suffering a willing sacrifice for his well-being. Her selfless love is shown by her acceptance of physical fading if it means he remains in a good state.

ai.literal: Pallor saying name obtaining is good indeed, he who caused love's not granting they slander not if.
ai.translation: It is good indeed to be known merely as "the pale one", as long as people do not slander the unkindness of the one who made me love him.
ai.modern: என் மீது அன்பு கொள்ளச் செய்த காதலர் இப்போது எனக்கு அன்பு காட்டாததை ஊரார் பழித்துத் தூற்றமாட்டார்கள் என்றால், நான் பசலை நோய் கொண்டவள் என்று பெயர் பெறுவது எனக்கு நல்லதே ஆகும்.
ai.explanation: The heroine is suffering from the physical signs of lovesickness, known as pallor, because her lover is away. She knows that the townspeople will notice her condition and gossip about it. However, she prefers that they simply label her condition as a disease called "pallor" rather than blaming her lover for his absence and lack of grace. This shows her deep devotion, as she is willing to bear the physical suffering and the stigma of the illness as long as her lover's reputation remains untarnished.
